description: Table 2 is a two-column, four-row data table rendered as an image (no plot axes, no micrograph, no scale bar). The left column header reads "Phase" and the right column header reads "Vickers microhardness, HV", with a horizontal rule separating the header row from the data rows. The table lists four microstructural constituents of an Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low-density steel and their Vickers microhardness values: Austenite 275 ± 10 HV; δ-ferrite 314 ± 15 HV; α-ferrite 374 ± 10 HV; Martensite 438 ± 15 HV. The values are printed as mean ± scatter and increase monotonically down the column, so the softest phase is austenite and the hardest is martensite, with δ-ferrite intermediate and α-ferrite close to martensite. The whole content is legible; nothing is cropped or blurred. The table exists to give the hardness signature used to discriminate the phases seen in the micrographs: as the citing text states, "The phases were distinguished according to the Vickers microhardness as is presented in Table 2", and the same values underpin the H70–H100 solution-treatment series (700–1000 °C, 1 h) in which austenite, α-ferrite, δ-ferrite and martensite were identified by their hardness.

subfigures.description: Two-column table with headers 'Phase' and 'Vickers microhardness, HV'. Rows: Austenite 275 ± 10; δ-ferrite 314 ± 15; α-ferrite 374 ± 10; Martensite 438 ± 15. A horizontal rule separates header from data; all text is legible.

observations.observation: Table 2 has exactly two columns, headed 'Phase' and 'Vickers microhardness, HV'.
The table lists four phases in the printed order: Austenite, δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, Martensite.
Austenite is printed with the lowest Vickers microhardness, 275 ± 10 HV.
Martensite is printed as 438 ± 15 HV, the highest value in the table.
The caption states the table gives the Vickers microhardness of different phases.
The citing text states the phases were distinguished according to the Vickers microhardness as presented in Table 2.

The citing text describes an Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low density steel solution treated at 700–1000 °C for 1 h, giving specimens H70, H80, H90 and H100 whose microstructures contain austenite, α-ferrite, δ-ferrite and martensite.
The table reports no measurement conditions (load, dwell time, indenter) and no per-sample breakdown; it is a phase-level hardness list only.
All four hardness values are printed as mean ± uncertainty, with the largest scatter (± 15) on δ-ferrite and martensite and the smallest (± 10) on austenite and α-ferrite.
